title: STM3: Mixture of Multiscale Mamba for Long-Term Spatio-Temporal Time-Series Prediction

problem.claim: Long-term spatio-temporal time-series prediction requires efficiently learning complex long-term spatio-temporal dependencies.

gap.claim: Existing methods struggle with efficient learning, while multiscale temporal information and correlations across nodes are difficult to extract and model.

contributions.claim: STM3 combines Multiscale Mamba with a Disentangled Mixture-of-Experts framework to capture diverse multiscale information and uses an adaptive graph causal network for spatial dependencies.
STM3 introduces stable routing and causal contrastive learning with hierarchical information aggregation to support robust, scale-distinguishable representations.
The authors provide theoretical results concerning routing smoothness and pattern disentanglement for each expert.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the Disentangled Mixture-of-Experts framework as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on 10 real-world benchmarks across domains with state-of-the-art results.
On PEMSD8, the authors report improvements over the second-best model of 7.1% in MAE, 8.5% in RMSE, and 15.9% in MAPE.
The authors report that code is available online.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-term spatio-temporal dependency learning is difficult for existing deep learning methods.
The task involves difficult multiscale temporal structure and correlated information across nodes.
STM3 combines multiscale Mamba, disentangled experts, adaptive graph causality, stable routing, contrastive learning, and hierarchical aggregation.
The authors state theoretical guarantees about routing smoothness and expert pattern disentanglement.
Experiments across 10 benchmarks and a PEMSD8 comparison are reported as demonstrating strong performance.

source_observation.claim: The method explicitly represents multiscale temporal information and separates patterns across experts.

interpretation.claim: When long-horizon data contain heterogeneous temporal scales, explicit scale-aware decomposition may improve modeling efficiency and distinguishability.

application.claim: Consider combining multiscale sequence processing with routing or expert mechanisms for long-term forecasting tasks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach benefits tasks lacking multiscale structure or strong cross-node correlations.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark identities, data splits, baselines, or statistical variability.
The abstract does not provide computational costs, ablations, or implementation details.
The theoretical proof assumptions and scope of the guarantees are not described.
